h2: Liquid penetrant testing in Detroit: production lines, field repairs and Michigan winters
html:
Liquid penetrant testing in Detroit: production lines, field repairs and Michigan winters

Liquid penetrant testing in Detroit falls into two kinds of work: penetrant lines inside plants that inspect castings and machined parts at production rate, and field PT on welds, repairs and non-magnetic components at plants and job sites. Atlantis sends field PT crews from Houston, writes and reviews PT procedures through an ASNT NDT Level III, and trains technicians for SNT-TC-1A certification.

Choosing a penetrant testing service. Most requests for liquid penetrant testing services come down to three choices, and a supplier should ask about all three before quoting:

  • Penetrant type: Type I fluorescent for higher sensitivity under UV-A light, or Type II visible red dye for field work where the area cannot be darkened.
  • Removal method: water-washable, post-emulsifiable (lipophilic or hydrophilic) or solvent-removable. Solvent removal suits spot checks on welds and repairs; post-emulsifiable systems suit production parts where fine cracks must not be washed out.
  • Sensitivity level and governing document: aerospace and many automotive part specifications call for a stated sensitivity level and ASTM E1417 process control, while pressure equipment usually follows ASME Section V Article 6 and the acceptance criteria of the construction code.

ASTM E1417 also requires routine system checks on a known-defect panel and controls on UV-A intensity and ambient light at the inspection station. A supplier that runs a penetrant line should be able to show those records for the day your parts went through.

"Fluid immersion testing". This search usually means one of two things. On penetrant lines, parts are often dipped in penetrant, emulsifier or developer tanks instead of being sprayed, with drain and dwell times controlled by the procedure. In ultrasonic testing, immersion means the part and probe sit in a water tank so sound couples through the water, a setup used in production and laboratory testing of bar, tube and machined parts. Atlantis does field work with contact and automated UT rather than tank immersion; the ultrasonic testing page explains the difference.

Field PT in a Michigan winter. ASME Section V Article 6 sets a standard temperature range of 40 to 125°F (5 to 52°C) for the penetrant materials and the test surface. Outdoor work in a Detroit winter often falls below that, so the part must be warmed and held in range, or the procedure must be qualified at the lower temperature using the comparator block method Article 6 describes. A procedure written for summer work will not cover January along the Detroit River, and an auditor will check.

Who oversees the pressure work. Boilers in Michigan come under the Boiler Division of the Bureau of Construction Codes in the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs. Michigan also runs its own OSHA-approved State Plan, which covers most private-sector workplaces. PT on a boiler or vessel repair forms part of the repair documentation the inspector reviews, so the procedure, technician certification and penetrant batch numbers should be recorded with the result.

The method is explained on the penetrant testing page, and PT is one of the services under conventional NDT. A low-temperature or production PT procedure can be written and qualified through NDT procedure development. Technicians can train through PT training, practice on the Practical NDT penetrant simulator, and find local enrollment on the Detroit NDT training page. To scope field PT, send the component list, materials and dates through the Detroit PT request.
